Therefore, for the destruction of saṃsāra, one should meditate upon her who is the witness and whose nature is the Self, with a mind devoid of mental constructs and joined in yoga.
Henceforth, O best of mountains, I shall describe the expansion of the outer worship; listen with an attentive mind.
Thus ends the ninth chapter of the Devīgītā;
thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter of the Devīgītā in the seventh book of the Śrī Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa.
Chapter Ten.
The Seventh Book: Now the Fortieth Chapter.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
Having risen in the morning, one should visualize a radiant lotus upon the head;
there, one should remember the venerable Guru in his own form, with the luster of camphor.
Having paid homage to the goddess, who is exceedingly serene, adorned with shimmering ornaments, and joined with her power (śakti), the wise one should then meditate upon Kuṇḍalinī.
I take refuge in that woman whose nature is bliss, who shines forth on the first departure, who becomes like nectar upon the return journey, and who moves within along the path.

Having meditated thus, one should meditate upon me in the center of that crest-lock as having the nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss; then, one should complete all the three duties beginning with purification.
Then, having offered the *agnihotra* for the sake of my pleasure, that best of the twice-born,
remaining on his own seat at the conclusion of the oblation, should perform the ritual resolve (*saṅkalpa*) for worship.
Having first performed the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and the placement of the Mātṛkās (mātṛkānyāsa),
one should always perform the placement of the Mātṛkās along with the Hṛllekhā mantra.
One should place the syllable *ha* at the *mūlādhāra*, the syllable *ra* at the heart,
likewise the syllable *ī* between the eyebrows, and the syllable *hrīṃ* on the crown of the head.
One should perform all other nyāsas prescribed by their respective mantras;
furthermore, one should again conceive of a seat within one's own body through the [elements] beginning with dharma.
Then, when [the mind] has been expanded by means of breath-control (prāṇāyāma),
the wise one should meditate upon the Great Goddess in the lotus of the heart, my own abode, upon a seat of five corpses.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
these five great pretas stand at the soles of my feet.
For these [beings] consist of the five elements and also consist of the five states;
but I, being of the nature of unmanifest consciousness, am in every way beyond them.
Then, having always become the seat [of the deities] within the Śaktitantras,
one should worship me with these mental enjoyments after meditating thus, and should also recite the mantra.
Having offered the recitation to the Śrī-devī, one should then perform the installation of the *arghya* water;
having arranged the vessels, one should purify the materials for worship.
Having first performed the binding of the directions with that water, with the *manu*, and with the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*), the preceptor should thereafter bow to the gurus.
Having received his permission, [one should then] take up my divine and heart-stealing form, which resides within the heart, upon the external seat.
Then, one should invoke [the deity] upon the seat by means of the vidyā for the stabilization of the vital breath (prāṇasthāpana);
likewise, there should be the invocation of the seat, the offering of water (arghya), water for the feet (pādya), and so forth, as well as water for sipping (ācamana).
Having offered with one's own devotion to the Goddess a bath, two garments, all kinds of ornaments, and appropriate fragrances and flowers; Dg_10.17 = DbhP_7,40.17.
One should properly perform the worship of the enclosures situated within the yantra;
for those who are unable to do so at every occasion, Friday is prescribed as the fixed time.
The deities of the limbs should be visualized as having forms of light identical to that of Mūladevī;
one should also contemplate the three worlds as being pervaded by a mass of that light.
One should worship the Root Goddess together with her retinue,
using fragrant substances such as perfumes and likewise well-scented flowers.
One should satisfy me with food offerings, libations, betel leaves, sacrificial fees, and so forth,
and also with this thousand-name hymn composed by you.

O Lord, I [protect myself] with the *Kavaca* hymn, with the verse beginning "I [am protected] by the Rudras," with the mantras of the *Devī-atharvaśiras*, and with those arising from the *Hṛllekhā-upaniṣad*.
With the great mantras of the Great Vidyā, a person whose heart is moistened by love should repeatedly please me and ask forgiveness from the Mother of the World.
With all his limbs marked by horripilation, his voice choked with tears in his eyes,
he should repeatedly please me with the sounds of dancing, singing, and other such performances.
Since I am indeed to be propounded by the complete study of the Vedas as well as all the Purāṇas, one should therefore please me with those.
One should constantly offer even one's own entire possession, including one's body;
thereafter, one should perform the perpetual fire sacrifice and [make offerings] to Brahmins and married women.
One should feed the *baṭukas*, the commoners, and others with the thought that they are the Goddess;
having bowed, one should then dismiss them from one's own heart in reverse order.
O observer of excellent vows, you should perform all worship to me with the Hṛllekhā mantra;
Hṛllekhā is remembered as the supreme leader of all mantras.
I am eternally reflected in the mirror of Hṛllekhā;
therefore, whatever is offered by Hṛllekhā is presented by all the mantras.
Having worshipped the Guru with ornaments and other offerings, one should attain the state of having fulfilled one's purpose;
whoever thus worships the Goddess Śrīmad-Bhuvanasundarī.
Indeed, for him nothing whatsoever is difficult to obtain anywhere at any time;
at the end of the body, he certainly goes to my Jewel Island in every way.
"He should be known as having the very nature of the Goddess; the gods always bow down to him.
Thus, O King, I have described to you the worship of the Great Goddess.
Having reflected upon this in its entirety, yet in accordance with your specific capacity, perform my worship; by that, you shall achieve your purpose.
But this Gītā scripture, one should never speak of it to one who is not a disciple;
it must not be given to one who lacks devotion, nor to a rogue, nor to one of evil intent.
This revelation is the uncovering of the mother’s breasts;
therefore, this must always be guarded with diligent effort.
It should indeed be given to a devoted disciple, to an eldest son,
and to one who is well-behaved, well-attired, and endowed with devotion to the Goddess.
One should recite this in the presence of the brahmins at the time of the śrāddha;
then all those ancestors, being satisfied, proceed to the supreme state.
Vyāsa said:
Having spoken thus, that Blessed Lady vanished right there;
and all the gods became joyful from the sight of the Goddess.
Then that goddess Haimavatī was born on Himālaya;
she who was known as Gaurī was given in marriage to Śaṅkara.
Then Skanda was born, and by him Tāraka was struck down.
O lord of men, previously, during the churning of the ocean, jewels appeared.
Thereupon, the goddess Ramā, praised by the gods with devotion for the sake of attaining Lakṣmī,
emerged from that place in order to bestow her grace upon them.
Vaikuṇṭha was granted [the boon] by the gods, and by that means his peace was restored.
Thus, O King, has this supreme majesty of the Goddess been narrated to you.
This subject concerning the manifestation of Gaurī and Lakṣmī, which grants all desires,
must not be spoken to anyone else, for it is a secret that has been revealed [only to you].
This Gītā is the very secret; it must be guarded with great effort.
O sinless one, everything that you asked has been told by me.
It is pure, purifying, and divine; what more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the tenth chapter of the Devīgītā; the Devīgītā is complete—thus ends the fortieth chapter of the Devīgītā in the seventh book of the Śrī Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa.
